title: Account for inflight client-side truncation and resume offsets in metering
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several customers and internal QA discovered cases where client-side truncation of streaming responses (user cancels/refreshes, or mobile clients drop to background) followed by a resume leads to incorrect token accounting: either double-charging (server credits resumed fragments again) or under-counting (server discards resumed fragments if it thinks they were already charged). The problem appears when clients send a resume request with an offset that is not aligned to the server's last committed token checkpoint, or when clients truncate locally and replay a prefix that differs at token boundaries due to tokenization/UCS normalization differences. This ticket implements robust resume-aware metering anchored to idempotent checkpoints and heuristics to detect client truncation + replay patterns.
proposal: Introduce a resume semantics extension to the streaming protocol where clients MAY include a 'Resume-Anchor' token-id and an approximate byte-offset. The metering pipeline will: (1) maintain per-session committed checkpoints (token-id + hash of last N tokens) that are anchored in the ledger, (2) on resume, reconcile client's anchor against the last committed checkpoint and compute delta tokens to bill, (3) if anchor mismatch within a small tolerance, run a conservative diff heuristic (compute longest common suffix/prefix of tokenized sequences) and bill only the non-overlapping suffix, (4) if heuristics cannot resolve (ambiguous or large mismatch), mark session for manual audit and apply a conservative 'no-double-charge' policy by not recharging until server receives explicit finalization. Add instrumentation and an audit endpoint to replay raw fragments for debugging.
implementation_steps: 1) Add 'Resume-Anchor' and 'Client-Offset' optional headers to WS/HTTP streaming API and document in API spec (doc link below).
2) Extend session metadata in metering service to persist committed_checkpoint {token_id, rolling_hash} and last_finalized_index. Store checkpoints in ledger shards for idempotency across reconnects.

3) Implement a reconcile routine: given client_anchor and incoming fragment, align tokens using server tokenizer, compare rolling_hash, compute billed_delta = tokens_after_checkpoint minus any overlap. Ensure deterministic outcome even if tokenization differences occur by using N-gram rolling hash of raw bytes for fallback.
4) Add conservative fallback: when mismatch > threshold (e.g., >64 tokens or hash distance high) do not re-bill and flag for audit; emit metric metering.resume.mismatch_count with tags.
5) Update billing ledger finalizer to accept 'resume_reconciliation' events and attach proof references (checkpoint id, fragment ids) so an auditor can re-run reconciliation offline.
6) Backfill: write a migration to populate committed_checkpoint for active sessions that do not have it, using last written fragments where available; migrate within a feature-flag window.
7) Add unit tests for reconcile routine, fuzz tests with different tokenizers/normalizations, and an e2e test simulating client truncation -> resume across WS, HTTP and gRPC.
8) Deploy behind feature flag; canary on 5% of traffic, monitor metering.resume.* metrics and billing divergence dashboards, then roll to 25/50/100%.
9) Run a dry-audit pass comparing new reconciliation billing to historical records to measure regression and false positives.
10) Rollout documentation and SDK updates showing how clients should send Resume-Anchor for best results.
tests: Unit: deterministic reconcile cases (aligned, off-by-1-token, tokenization-difference)
Fuzz: random text truncation/resume with different encodings (UTF-8 multi-byte boundaries) and mobile client patterns
Integration: simulate 10k concurrent sessions with intermittent disconnects and resumes; assert ledger invariants and no double-charging in 99.999% of cases
E2E: synthetic traffic replaying field incidents reported by support to ensure fixes address reproduced issues
acceptance_criteria: Reproduction: we can consistently reproduce the reported double-charge/under-charge in a local harness and show the new reconcile routine fixes it
Metrics: metering.resume.mismatch_count drops to <1% of resumed sessions after rollout and audit flags are actionable
Billing correctness: manual audit of a 500-session sample shows no overcharges attributable to resume path after rollout
Performance: 99th percentile server-side resume latency increase < 5ms on affected codepaths when feature flag on
No regressions: existing non-resume flows (fresh streams) show no change in token counts and unit tests pass
